thread:
rahul: spun up a tiny canary for quark-lite-int6 on the onboarding fleet. Overall conv: pretty close to baseline for short responses but we’re seeing a recurring "toolcall" parse-failure class where trailing objects are truncated in streaming mode.

izzy: example from traces:
```
{"tool":"create_incident","args":{"desc":"payment failed","user":456}}
...<cut>
```
parser: unexpected EOF while parsing object

dana: is this only for function/tool calling outputs or general structured JSON? any difference with embeddings/regular completions?

rahul: so far isolated to tool outputs (funcall style). Regular completions fine. Non-streaming replication looked clean in a 200-sample check.

liam: could be our streaming boundary handler dropping the final chunk when tokenization hits a kernel tiling edge in int6 path. saw similar with other microquant builds.

izzy: can we prove streaming vs kernel? try forcing sync-mode for a subset and replay failing prompts.

rahul: doing that now — flipping 15% of canary to sync-mode and enabling minimal client repair heuristic for canary-only (append closing braces/brackets if safe). will also enable masked-last-10-token logging for failures.

ops-bot: canary-deploy quark-lite-int6 -> 2026-03-29T11:12:19Z (id: f9a8c)

dana: also proposal: one internal retry on parse-fail that forces sync-mode and does not consume user retry budget for canary. If retry succeeds, mark as 'repair-win' metric.

liam: add metrics: funcall_parse_fail_rate, repair_win_rate, last_chunk_len, kernel_evict_count. dashboard tile pls.

rahul: plan: 1) sync-mode probe 15% (in flight), 2) client-side healer for canary, 3) single internal sync retry on long responses, 4) capture masked suffix. i'll run a small eval comparing pass rate across float/int8/int6 over 1h and post diffs.

izzy: if sync-mode removes the failures that points strongly at streaming/path specific issue. then microquant rebuild with kernel alignment fix is next.

dana: also check worker preemptions and VM evictions in the same windows. if preempt spikes line up, we may need stronger final-chunk persistence.

liam: thanks — will prepare a short unit test to simulate duplicate-eos and dropped-final-chunk cases so future builds catch regressions.

rahul: perfect. will update in 45m with harness output. keep canary tight. :eyes:
